new-phyrexia.significance:
- significance: >-
      Sheoldred's Dominaria United printing represents the praetor directing
      the sleeper-agent infiltration that preceded the wider invasion.

- significance: >-
      A Phyrexian-language printing of the compleated Ajani, illustrating
      the betrayal that cost the Dominarian resistance one of its heroes.

- significance: >-
      Norn's original Phyrexia: All Will Be One portrait, an emblem of the
      Machine Orthodoxy's attempt to impose a single will on every plane.

- significance: >-
      The corrupted Nissa shows the personal cost of the failed strike team
      and the danger of compleation that could preserve a planeswalker's spark.

- significance: >-
      A Phyrexia: All Will Be One promotional printing portraying Koth,
      the Mirran resistance leader who never abandoned his home.

- significance: >-
      The original New Phyrexia portrait of the blue-aligned praetor,
      whose obsession with experimentation later enabled compleation
      of planeswalkers without extinguishing their sparks.

- significance: >-
      The original depiction of the predatory green praetor.
      Vorinclex later stole World Tree essence from Kaldheim,
      creating the foundation for Realmbreaker's growth.

- significance: >-
      A 2023 Multiverse Legends portrait of the red praetor whose
      furnace tolerated Mirran refugees. It recalls his earlier
      opposition to Norn, not a separate invasion-era persona.

- significance: >-
      Melira's original New Phyrexia card depicts the Mirran
      immune to Phyrexian contamination, a resistance fighter
      whose last intervention later saved Ajani and Nissa.

- significance: >-
      The original Kamigawa: Neon Dynasty illustration of
      a compleated planeswalker. Tamiyo's later final story
      distinguishes her lost body from the magical memory
      that survived to console her family.

march-of-the-machine.significance:
- significance: >-
      The machinery of interplanar invasion, grown from stolen World Tree
      essence and used to open passages for Phyrexia's armies.

- significance: >-
      A Battle card documenting one of many simultaneous fronts, where
      Realmbreaker's branches struck the World Tree and its realms.

- significance: >-
      Chandra's March of the Machine portrait marks her determination
      to continue the fight after the Seedcore mission's failure.

- significance: >-
      Wrenn's union with the invasion tree transforms Phyrexia's instrument
      of conquest into a path for Zhalfir's liberation.

- significance: >-
      A borderless illustration of Elspeth's angelic return, portraying
      the figure who confronted Norn at the climax of the invasion.

- significance: >-
      A double-faced Battle card depicting the counterattack on New Phyrexia
      and Teferi's return with Zhalfir's forces.

- significance: >-
      An Aftermath-era image of Karn after the war, linking the defeat of
      New Phyrexia to the fate of the plane he originally created.

- significance: >-
      The original Kamigawa: Neon Dynasty illustration of
      a compleated planeswalker. Tamiyo's later final story
      distinguishes her lost body from the magical memory
      that survived to console her family.
